title: Authorization server metadata omits `code_challenge_methods_supported`
rationale: Until 29 July 2026 this fixture asserted a violation, and its own rationale gave the argument R1 exists to reject: that the sentence 'states the client's obligation rather than the server's, but the observable is on the server'. That is the reasoning C16 was made descriptive-only to refuse, and the reasoning MCP's Resource Indicators clause was already rejected for. Reading the primary text settled it: RFC 8414 marks the element OPTIONAL, and RFC 9700 (BCP 240) 2.1.1 -- the only text bridging 'authorization servers MUST support PKCE' to advertising it -- sets that bridge at RECOMMENDED and expressly permits 'a deployment-specific way' instead, which no passive prober can observe. So an absent element is not evidence that any authorization-server MUST was violated. The one server-binding MUST that exists (MCP 2025-11-25, conditioned on OpenID Connect Discovery) is absent from MCP 2025-06-18, which R7 makes the governing revision. The element is still read and still reported; only the verdict class changed.

spec.quote:
code_challenge_methods_supported
      OPTIONAL.  JSON array containing a list of Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) [RFC7636] code challenge methods supported by this authorization server. ... If omitted, the authorization server does not support PKCE.

Authorization servers MUST provide a way to detect their support for PKCE. It is RECOMMENDED for authorization servers to publish the element code_challenge_methods_supported in their Authorization Server Metadata [RFC8414] containing the supported PKCE challenge methods (which can be used by the client to detect PKCE support). Authorization servers MAY instead provide a deployment-specific way to ensure or determine PKCE support by the authorization server.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org and datatracker, 29 July 2026

spec.quote: If `code_challenge_methods_supported` is absent, the authorization server does not support PKCE and MCP clients MUST refuse to proceed.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified 29 July 2026; binds the CLIENT, and is absent from revision 2025-06-18, which R7 makes the governing revision
